question: What is the main goal of Behavioural Change Communication (BCC) in public health?

options.A: To promote positive and healthy behaviour choices
options.B: To replace modern medicine with traditional remedies
options.C: To distribute free medical equipment to hospitals
options.D: To punish communities that ignore health guidelines

explanation: Spot on! BCC is all about working together with individuals and communities to help them build healthier lifestyle habits. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T3#GNS124_U5_T3_h1)

question: How is BCC different from standard, one-way health talks?

options.A: BCC focuses only on treating emergency trauma patients
options.B: BCC relies exclusively on television and radio broadcasts
options.C: BCC uses interactive dialogue instead of just giving information
options.D: BCC avoids talking directly with community members

explanation: You got it! While basic education just throws facts at people, BCC gets a conversation going so we can truly understand and address their concerns. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T3#GNS124_U5_T3_h1)

question: Which model explains that people change their habits by moving through steps like thinking about it, and then finally taking action?
explanation: Well done! The Transtheoretical Model breaks down the journey of change from early thoughts all the way to long-term maintenance. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T3#GNS124_U5_T3_h2)

question: According to the Health Belief Model, what pushes someone to finally adopt a new health habit?

options.A: Being forced by local law enforcement officers to visit the clinic
options.B: Forgetting that diseases exist in their local environment
options.C: Receiving financial payment for every health clinic visit
options.D: Believing the health threat is serious and the benefits outweigh the barriers

explanation: Exactly! People are ready to make a change when they see a real personal risk and feel that the solution is easy enough to do. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T3#GNS124_U5_T3_h2)

question: Why is it smart for a nurse to involve religious leaders and local heads in a community health plan?

options.A: To dispense prescription antibiotics to villagers
options.B: To gain community buy-in and policy support
options.C: To diagnose complex medical surgical conditions
options.D: To audit hospital financial expenditure records

explanation: Spot on! Local leaders have great influence over the people, so having their backing helps the community welcome new health programs. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T3#GNS124_U5_T3_h3)

question: You want to launch an immunization campaign in a rural village. Which approach shows a great BCC strategy?

options.A: Posting English warning signs in markets where people cannot read English
options.B: Waiting quietly at the clinic for patients to walk in by themselves
options.C: Partnering with local women's groups and trusted peer educators for dialogue
options.D: Publishing dense medical research papers in international journals

explanation: Brilliant choice! Working with trusted local groups and talking face-to-face always beats sitting back and waiting or using confusing posters. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T3#GNS124_U5_T3_h3)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do when starting a Behavioural Change Communication project?
explanation: Correct! Before designing any messages, you have to talk to the community to find out what they already know and what they actually need. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T3#GNS124_U5_T3_h4)

question: Why must nurses pre-test health posters and flyers with the local community before printing thousands of copies?

options.A: To calculate the exact salary of the project nurses and staff
options.B: To guarantee that the printed posters are waterproof and durable
options.C: To ensure the messages are culturally appropriate and easily understood
options.D: To comply with international tax laws for healthcare projects

explanation: Spot on! Pre-testing saves you from printing confusing or offensive messages by catching misunderstandings early. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T3#GNS124_U5_T3_h4)

question: Why is BCC so important in programs like malaria control?

options.A: People must be persuaded to consistently sleep under insecticide-treated nets
options.B: BCC automatically kills adult mosquitoes living near stagnant water pools
options.C: Insects understand health messages broadcasted over local radio stations
options.D: Communication programs replace the need for antimalarial drug treatments

explanation: You got it! Having mosquito nets in a box doesn't help if people refuse to hang and sleep under them every night. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T3#GNS124_U5_T3_h5)

question: Your clinic has free cholera vaccines, but villagers are refusing them because of scary rumours. What should you do?

options.A: Close the clinic permanently and transfer the nursing staff to a city
options.B: Use BCC strategies like town hall meetings to address rumors and build trust
options.C: Call the police to force every single villager to receive the injection
options.D: Ignore the rumours and wait for people to figure out the truth alone

explanation: Exactly! Open dialogue and town hall meetings help clear up dangerous myths and build confidence in public health care. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T3#GNS124_U5_T3_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to changing health habits in local communities?

options.A: Cultural beliefs and traditional illness explanations
options.C: Excessive availability of free clinical resources
options.D: Distrust of the formal healthcare system

explanation: Spot on! Having plenty of free resources helps health programs succeed. Poverty, cultural myths, and distrust are the real hurdles we face. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T3#GNS124_U5_T3_h6)

question: Why might a mother fail to feed her child recommended healthy foods even after a great health talk?

options.A: She may lack the financial resources to buy the recommended food items
options.B: She forgot that human beings require food to survive daily
options.C: She deliberately wants her children to suffer from malnutrition
options.D: She prefers reading medical textbooks instead of cooking meals

explanation: Correct! Even when mothers want the best for their kids, lack of money can be a major roadblock to acting on healthy advice. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T3#GNS124_U5_T3_h6)

question: What is the main difference between monitoring and evaluating a health communication program?

options.A: Monitoring costs money, while evaluation is always completely free
options.B: Monitoring is done by patients, while evaluation is done by politicians
options.C: Monitoring tracks daily activities, while evaluation measures long-term impact
options.D: Monitoring focuses on drugs, while evaluation focuses only on surgery

explanation: Well done! Monitoring looks at what is happening day-to-day, while evaluation checks the overall success at the end. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T3#GNS124_U5_T3_h7)

question: Why do nurses compare data collected after a health campaign with the baseline numbers gathered before it started?

options.A: To satisfy personal curiosity about how many posters were printed
options.B: To determine if the health campaign actually caused positive behavior changes
options.C: To calculate the exact travel expenses of the visiting health team
options.D: To prove that no one in the community attended any health meetings

explanation: Spot on! Comparing 'before' and 'after' numbers is the only way to prove whether your awareness campaign truly made a difference. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T3#GNS124_U5_T3_h7)
